title: myColorado app cybersecurity incident, Nov 2026

subject.name: myColorado
subject.about: myColorado is the State of Colorado's mobile app. People use it to carry a mobile driver license and the Colorado Digital ID on their phone, and to reach some state services.

disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by the State of Colorado, any news outlet, regulator, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: One statewide app with about 2.1 million users, offline for everyone. The state estimates roughly 100,000 users' data was involved, mainly uploaded documents; the count is still being refined.
who_is_affected: Everyone who uses the myColorado app for a digital driver license, digital ID or state services. Carry your physical ID, including for holiday flights. The state expects to start notifying people whose documents were involved on Nov 27.

known.text: The state says an unauthorized user accessed myColorado platform data, found late on Nov 18.
The state shut the app down and it is still unavailable, with no restoration date.
The state estimates roughly 100,000 users' data was involved.
The state says photos and PDFs of documents such as passports, vehicle registrations and insurance cards were accessed; payment information was not.
State services are still available through agency websites, and a physical ID is needed meanwhile.

not_known.text: Exactly whose documents were involved: the state is still matching them to users.
Who got in, and through what vulnerability.
